name: Vuorio's Universe and Warped Anti-de Sitter Space
description: An empty space of gravity in three dimensions with a mass for the graviton, whose time twists about every point. It is anti-de Sitter space with its light cones stretched or squashed along one direction, and stretched, as in Vuorio's universe, it holds closed timelike curves through every event.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit, take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and write a dot in the geodesic equations for a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Vuorio's universe is empty, and still it is curved, with closed timelike curves through every one of its events [vuorio1985, rooman1998]. In a world with two dimensions of space that takes a new kind of gravity, since Einstein's theory there has no gravitational waves and leaves empty space flat wherever matter is absent [deser1982, deser1982annals]. A new term in the action changes that, one "of topological origin", which Stanley Deser, Roman Jackiw, and S. Templeton added in 1982 [deser1982annals]. With it, they wrote, gravity "acquires a propagating, massive, spin 2 mode", and the theory stays free of ghosts and causal, though its field equations carry three derivatives of the metric [deser1982annals]. Topologically massive gravity, as the theory came to be called, has curved vacua, and Vuorio's universe is one of them [percacci1987].¶The solution came out of the Center for Theoretical Physics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1985, where Ilkka Vuorio presented "a stationary, radially symmetric vacuum solution" [vuorio1985]. Nothing fills it, and its time is twisted, so that the light cones tip over farther the farther they stand from any one point, as they do in Kurt Gödel's rotating universe [vuorio1985, rooman1998]. Vuorio identified "all four Killing vectors" of the spacetime and solved its geodesic equation [vuorio1985]. The twist is tied to the graviton's mass, a third of it, and Vuorio worked in units that made that mass three [gurses2010, moussa2003]. Far enough from any point the circles about it are closed timelike curves, beyond $\sinh^2(\Omega r/2) = 1/3$ in the cylindrical chart [reboucas2009, moussa2003].¶Two years later Vuorio, with Roberto Percacci and Pasquale Sodano, wrote down the field equations for every stationary metric, found that "all these metrics have a nonvanishing twist", and gave every solution whose twist is constant [percacci1987]. The twist measures, in their words, "the angular velocity by which neighboring orbits" of the time direction "rotate around each other", and without it the only stationary vacuum is flat space [percacci1987]. The homogeneous vacua that admit a cosmological constant are, in Yavuz Nutku's phrase, "only Vuorio-type solutions" [nutku1993]. Metin Gürses showed in 1994 that a class of Einstein's metrics with perfect fluid sources also solves the theory with a cosmological constant [gurses1994], and later tied the family to Gödel's universe [gurses2010]. They are the homogeneous metrics of Gödel's type that Marcelo Rebouças and Jayme Tiomno had found in 1983, a timelike line twisted over a hyperbolic plane of curvature $-m^2$, and each solves the theory with the twist $\Omega$ a third of the graviton's mass and the cosmological constant $\Lambda = (\Omega^2 - m^2)/3$ [reboucas1983, gurses2010]. Vuorio's universe is the member $m = \Omega$, with no cosmological constant, and Gödel's universe, less its flat direction, is the member $m^2 = 2\Omega^2$ [reboucas2009].¶Why should an empty space behave like a universe of rotating dust? Marianne Rooman and Philippe Spindel answered with a picture [rooman1998]. The light cones of the whole family are those of anti-de Sitter space, tilted, and squashed or stretched along one direction, with anti-de Sitter space itself at "the boundary between causally safe and causally pathological spaces" [rooman1998]. Stretched, as in Vuorio's universe and in Gödel's, the cones open wide enough to hold closed timelike curves through every event [rooman1998, moussa2003]. Light sent out from one event then spirals out to a caustic circle and comes back together [rooman1998]. In the squashed spaces Rooman and Spindel found no causal pathology [rooman1998].¶The name warped anti-de Sitter space is due to Dionysios Anninos, Wei Li, Megha Padi, Wei Song, and Andrew Strominger, who went looking for vacua of the theory other than anti-de Sitter space [anninos2009]. Anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions is a line fibred over anti-de Sitter space of two, and in a warped space that fibre carries a constant factor, which stretches it when $\mu\ell > 3$ and squashes it below, with $\mu$ the graviton's mass and $\Lambda = -1/\ell^2$ [anninos2009]. The fibre may be timelike, as in Vuorio's universe, or spacelike [anninos2009]. The spacelike stretched spaces hold black holes, and Anninos and his coauthors showed them to be quotients of warped anti-de Sitter space, "just as BTZ black holes are" quotients of anti-de Sitter space [anninos2009]. Black holes had come out of Vuorio's own solution in 2003, when Karim Ait Moussa, Gérard Clément, and Cédric Leygnac continued it analytically into spacetimes in which "no observers can remain static" [moussa2003]. David Chow, Christopher Pope, and Ergin Sezgin later sorted the known solutions of the theory into one classification, with Vuorio's written in his own coordinates [chow2010].¶The same spaces turn up beside the horizon of a black hole spinning as fast as it can [bengtsson2006, bardeen1999]. Ingemar Bengtsson and Patrik Sandin studied the squashed and stretched spaces for the sake of the extremal Kerr black hole, whose near horizon geometry at constant Boyer-Lindquist latitude "is anti-de Sitter space squashed along compactified spacelike fibres" [bengtsson2006]. Near the poles the fibres are squashed, at about $47°$ from the axis the slice is plain anti-de Sitter space, and closer to the equator it is stretched [bengtsson2006]. They also found that stretching along a timelike fibre traps the null geodesics inside the spacetime and that squashing lets them out, and argued that either one destroys the conformal boundary anti-de Sitter space has [bengtsson2006]. With the spin then reported for the black hole in Sagittarius, $J/M^2 = 0.9939$, they concluded "that to a very good approximation there are squashed anti-de Sitter spaces at the centre of the Milky Way" [bengtsson2006].

related.text: Kurt Gödel's rotating universe of dust. Less its flat direction it is the member $m^2 = 2\Omega^2$ of this family, a vacuum of topologically massive gravity [reboucas2009, gurses2010].
Anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions is the member $m = 2\Omega$, where the cones are neither squashed nor stretched and the closed timelike curves are gone [rooman1998, boyda2003].
Charged dust in rigid rotation. Its plane of $t$, $r$, and $\phi$ twists a flat plane where this family twists a hyperbolic one, Rebouças and Tiomno's line element at $m = 0$ [reboucas2009].

The throat of the extreme Kerr black hole. Each of its slices of constant latitude is anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions warped along a spacelike circle, squashed near the axis and stretched near the equator [bengtsson2006].
The black hole of anti-de Sitter space in three dimensions, a quotient of it. The black holes of spacelike warped anti-de Sitter space are quotients of that space in the same way [anninos2009].
Gravity in three dimensions without a mass for the graviton, where a particle makes a cone and empty space stays flat [deser1982annals].

The spinning particle of gravity in three dimensions, drawn out along a line into a string. Its closed timelike curves wind close about the source, and this universe's lie beyond a fixed distance from every point [reboucas2009].

coordinates.name: Cylindrical
domains: \tanh\left(\dfrac{mr}{2}\right) = \dfrac{m}{2\Omega} \;\text{(for } m < 2\Omega\text{, the circle of constant } t, r \text{ is null)}
\tanh\left(\dfrac{mr}{2}\right) > \dfrac{m}{2\Omega} \;\text{(the circles of constant } t, r \text{ are closed timelike curves)}

parameters.description: Twist of the Killing vector $\partial_t$, an inverse length; the graviton's topological mass is $\mu = 3\Omega$

Curvature scale of the plane that $\partial_t$ turns about, an inverse length, so that its Gaussian curvature is $-m^2$; the cosmological constant is $\Lambda = (\Omega^2 - m^2)/3$, and Vuorio's universe is $m = \Omega$

coordinates.convention: We use Rebouças and Tiomno's cylindrical coordinates $(t, r, \phi)$ about one integral curve of $\partial_t$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $r$ the proper distance from that curve, and $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$.

coordinates.name: Poincaré disc
domains: R = \dfrac{m}{2\Omega} \;\text{(for } m < 2\Omega\text{, the circle of constant } t, R \text{ is null)}
R > \dfrac{m}{2\Omega} \;\text{(the circles of constant } t, R \text{ are closed timelike curves)}

parameters.description: Twist of the Killing vector $\partial_t$, an inverse length; the graviton's topological mass is $\mu = 3\Omega$

Curvature scale of the plane that $\partial_t$ turns about, an inverse length, so that its Gaussian curvature is $-m^2$; the cosmological constant is $\Lambda = (\Omega^2 - m^2)/3$, and Vuorio's universe is $m = \Omega$

coordinates.convention: We use Bengtsson and Sandin's coordinates $(t, R, \phi)$ on Poincaré's disc, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $R = \tanh(mr/2)$ dimensionless, and $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$.
geodesics: \ddot{t} + \dfrac{8\Omega^2\,R}{m^2\left(1 + R\right)\left(1 - R\right)}\dot{t}\dot{R} + \dfrac{8\Omega\,R^3\left(2\Omega - m\right)\left(2\Omega + m\right)}{m^4\left(1 + R\right)^2\left(1 - R\right)^2}\dot{R}\dot{\phi} = 0

\ddot{R} + 2\Omega\,R\,\dot{t}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{2R}{\left(1 + R\right)\left(1 - R\right)}\dot{R}^2 + \dfrac{R\left(8\Omega^2\,R^2 - R^2\,m^2 - m^2\right)}{m^2\left(1 + R\right)\left(1 - R\right)}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0
